TRADING PLATFORM GUIDE // PARTNER

Bitunix: what traders should know before opening an account

A practical overview of the platform, its standard trading fees, futures and copy-trading mechanics, and the risks that matter. RWA Wire has an affiliate partnership with Bitunix, but this guide is designed to help you evaluate the platform rather than promise trading results.

Affiliate disclosure

If you create an account through links on this page, RWA Wire may receive a commission from eligible trading activity at no additional cost to you. This commercial relationship does not change the risks of trading and does not make Bitunix suitable for every reader. Availability and product access can vary by jurisdiction.

01 // OVERVIEW

What is Bitunix?

Bitunix is a crypto trading platform offering spot and derivatives markets. For RWA Wire readers, the relevant question is not whether an exchange is “best,” but whether its products, fee structure, execution, controls and regional availability fit the way you intend to trade.

02 // FEES

Standard trading fees

Bitunix currently lists the following VIP 0 maker/taker rates. Higher VIP tiers can have lower rates. Always verify the live fee page before trading because platform pricing can change.

MarketMakerTaker
Spot0.0800%0.1000%
Futures0.0200%0.0600%

Trading costs can also include funding, spreads, slippage and withdrawal/network costs depending on the product and transaction.

03 // FUTURES

Futures require a different risk framework

Perpetual futures allow leveraged exposure without owning the underlying asset. Leverage magnifies both gains and losses and can lead to liquidation. Before using futures, understand margin mode, liquidation price, funding rates, order types and the maximum amount of capital you are prepared to lose.

04 // COPY TRADING

Copy trading is automation, not risk removal

Bitunix supports futures copy trading. Copied positions remain futures positions and can be affected by trading fees, funding, slippage and profit sharing. The platform's current rules state that copy-trading leverage is capped at 10x and that followers can use fixed-amount or fixed-ratio modes. A lead trader's displayed historical return is not a guarantee of a follower's future result.

05 // CHECKLIST

Before creating an account

Confirm Bitunix is available where you live.
Read the current spot/futures fee schedule.
Understand custody and withdrawal procedures.
Enable the available account-security controls.
For futures, define leverage and liquidation risk first.
For copy trading, review drawdown — not only ROI.

RWA WIRE VIEW

Who might find the platform relevant?

The product set is most relevant to readers actively looking for crypto spot, futures or copy-trading functionality. Readers who only want to hold tokenized assets or follow institutional RWA developments do not need an exchange account simply because they read RWA Wire. Platform choice should follow the product you actually need.

06 // SOURCES & UPDATES

Verify live terms before trading

Fee schedules, product rules and regional access can change. This page is an editorial guide, not a substitute for Bitunix's current terms, risk disclosures or product documentation. RWA Wire will update material details when identified.
